title: Laid in a Manger
old_p1: Micah, a prophet who spoke for Heavenly Father, lived when Isaiah did. He said little Bethlehem would be special.
Micah said a great Ruler, a leader like a king, would come from there. Bethlehem was King David’s town.
Years later, the leader of Rome said all the people must be counted. So Joseph went to Bethlehem with Mary. Soon she would have a baby.
old_p2: In Bethlehem, baby Jesus was born! Mary wrapped Him snugly in soft cloths. There was no room for them in the inn, a place where travelers stay. So Mary laid Him in a manger, a box that holds food for animals.
Tonight, hug your pillow. You can make room for Jesus in your heart too.
p1: Long before the first Christmas, Micah promised that a great ruler would come from little Bethlehem. Many years later, Mary and Joseph traveled to that very town. They had come because the ruler of Rome wanted the people to be counted.
Mary was going to have a baby soon. The roads had been long, and Bethlehem was crowded with travelers. It was time for her child to be born.
p2: That night, baby Jesus was born. Mary wrapped Him snugly in cloths and laid Him in a manger, a little feeding place for animals. There was no room for them in the place where travelers stayed.

The promised Savior had arrived, not in a grand palace, but in a humble resting place. He came because Heavenly Father loves His children. Tonight, snuggle your pillow close and remember: there is always room to welcome Jesus in your heart.
note: Levi, 20 Nov 2026 ("Match up the story lantern stories with the published book"): p1 and p2 are the story words AS PRINTED in the published December book (We Have Waited for Him, on Amazon), first and second story page, word for word, so the Lantern, the app's Books page and the book a family bought read the same. The Christian edition reads God for Heavenly Father; p2_christian only where the printed words are Latter-day Saint teaching. The 29 Oct picture-book rewrite is kept as rewrite_p1/rewrite_p2.
rewrite_p1: Long ago, Micah told the people what Heavenly Father said. Bethlehem was a little town, but Micah said it would be special.
A great Ruler would come from Bethlehem, King David’s town. Micah was talking about Jesus!
Years later, a ruler named Caesar said everyone must be counted. Joseph was from David’s family, so he took Mary to Bethlehem.
rewrite_p2: While they were there, baby Jesus was born! Mary wrapped Him snugly in soft cloths. There was no room for them at the inn, where travelers stay. So Mary laid Him in a manger, a little feed box for animals.
Mary and Joseph made a cozy place for Jesus with love. Tonight, you can make room for Jesus in your heart too.
